The studio & the signal chain

We build instruments out of math.

Voltrove is a two-person workshop making playable synthesizers that need nothing but a browser. The Filament One is our first public instrument — here’s the story, and a tour of exactly how it turns a key-press into sound.

In 2023 we got tired of every “try our synth” button leading to a 400-megabyte installer. The web already has a real-time audio engine baked into it — the Web Audio API — so we asked a stubborn question: how much of a proper hardware-feeling synth can you ship as a single web page?

The answer turned out to be: almost all of it. The Filament One is a complete subtractive synthesizer. Two oscillators, an envelope-driven resonant filter, amplitude shaping, a stereo-feel feedback delay, a sixteen-step sequencer, and an oscilloscope — and it loads as fast as a blog post. We named it after the glowing tungsten filament of an old vacuum tube: warm, simple, and a little bit alive.

How a note becomes sound

When you press a key, the synth builds a fresh voice and routes it through this chain. Every box below is a real Web Audio node:

Oscillators ×2OscillatorNode
→
Amp ADSRGainNode
→
Resonant filterBiquadFilterNode
→
Drive + delayWaveShaper · DelayNode
→
Analyser → outAnalyserNode

1 · Oscillators

Two oscillators give the Filament One its body. Osc A sets the core character; Osc B sits underneath at a chosen octave and is blended in with the Osc B mix control. Nudging the Detune control spreads the two oscillators a few cents apart, which is the entire secret behind a “fat” analog sound — the slight beating between the two pitches is what your ear reads as richness.

2 · The amplitude envelope (ADSR)

Raw oscillators just drone. The ADSR envelope shapes their loudness over time: Attack is how fast the note fades in, Decay drops it to the Sustain level it holds while you keep the key down, and Release is the tail after you let go. Short attack + zero sustain gives a pluck; long attack + long release gives a pad. It’s the same four numbers behind almost every electronic sound you’ve ever heard.

3 · The resonant filter

A lowpass BiquadFilter removes the harmonics above its cutoff frequency — the higher the cutoff, the brighter the tone. Crank the resonance (Q) and the frequencies right at the cutoff get a sharp boost, the squelchy “wah” that defines acid basslines. A second envelope sweeps the cutoff each time you play, so notes open up and then settle — that’s the Filter envelope amount.

4 · Drive, delay & the master bus

From the filter, every voice sums into a shared bus. A gentle waveshaper adds Drive — soft saturation that thickens the sound. A feedback DelayNode creates echoes, with feedback deciding how many repeats and mix how loud they sit. Finally a compressor keeps big chords from clipping, an AnalyserNode feeds the oscilloscope you see while you play, and the signal reaches your speakers.

5 · The step sequencer’s secret: a lookahead clock

Naively scheduling notes with setInterval drifts and stutters, because JavaScript timers aren’t precise. The Filament One instead uses the classic lookahead scheduler: a lightweight timer wakes up every 25 ms only to schedule notes a fraction of a second ahead, but each note’s actual start time is locked to the rock-solid Web Audio hardware clock. The result is sample-accurate timing that never wanders, even while the tab is busy — and it’s how the optional swing control can shuffle the off-beats by exact amounts.

Specifications

SectionDetail
ArchitectureTwo-oscillator subtractive, polyphonic
OscillatorsSine · triangle · sawtooth · square, per-osc octave & detune
Filter12 dB/oct resonant lowpass with dedicated envelope
EnvelopesADSR for amplitude, separate envelope amount for filter
EffectsSoft-clip drive · feedback delay with damping · master limiter
Sequencer16 steps · 4 drum lanes · 1 synth lane · 40–200 BPM · swing
VisualizerReal-time oscilloscope + 1024-bin spectrum (FFT 2048)
StorageUnlimited user patches saved to browser localStorage
RequirementsAny browser with the Web Audio API — no installs, works offline
